questions.prompt: Tell me about yourself.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Can you tell a clear, logical story in about a minute that explains why you're sitting in this interview?
framework: Where you're from and what you study (one line)
The moment or experience that got you interested in finance
What you did about it — clubs, courses, jobs, self-study
What you learned the job involves and why it fits you
Why you're here today (this firm / role)
mustInclude: A clear thread connecting your experiences to banking
One or two specific actions, not a list of everything
A forward-looking close
avoid: Reading your resume line by line
Generic lines like "I've always loved finance"

builderFields.label: Where you're from + school + major
builderFields.hint: One sentence.

builderFields.label: What first got you interested in finance
builderFields.hint: A specific moment: a class, job, person, or event.

builderFields.label: What you did about it
builderFields.hint: Clubs, case comps, internships, self-study — pick the strongest 2.

builderFields.label: What you learned about the job, and why it fits you
builderFields.hint: Show you know what analysts actually do.

builderFields.label: Why you're interviewing here
builderFields.hint: One line tying to this firm or role.

questions.outlineTemplate: I'm a [year] at [school] studying [major], originally from [hometown]. I got interested in finance when [spark]. Since then I've [action 1] and [action 2], which showed me that [what the job involves]. That fits me because [strength]. That's why I'm excited about [role] at [firm].
likelyFollowUps: Why finance over [your major's usual path]?
Tell me more about [an experience you mentioned].

questions.prompt: Walk me through your resume.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Same as "tell me about yourself," but anchored to your resume. Can you connect the dots and explain your choices?
framework: Open with school and why you chose your major
Move through experiences in order, one or two lines each
For each, say why you did it and what you took from it
End with why banking is the logical next step
mustInclude: The reason behind each move
What each experience taught you that's relevant to banking
avoid: Spending equal time on everything — linger on the most relevant

builderFields.label: Experience 1: why you did it, what you learned
Experience 2: why you did it, what you learned
Why banking is the next step

questions.outlineTemplate: I chose [school/major] because [reason]. My first experience was [exp1], where I learned [lesson]. That led me to [exp2], where [lesson]. Those experiences pointed me toward banking because [reason], and that's what brings me here.
likelyFollowUps: Which experience was most valuable?
What would you do differently?

questions.prompt: What do you do outside of school and recruiting?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Are you a real, interesting person the team would want to work with at 1 a.m.?
framework: Name one or two genuine interests
Add a specific detail that makes it memorable
Optionally connect it to a trait (discipline, teamwork)
mustInclude: Specific detail ("I've run three half marathons" beats "I like running")
avoid: Saying you have no time for hobbies
Listing five hobbies with no detail
questions.outlineTemplate: Outside of class I [interest] — [specific detail]. It's taught me [trait].
likelyFollowUps: How did you get into that?

questions.prompt: Why investment banking?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Do you understand what an analyst actually does, and is there a believable reason you want that job specifically?
framework: What sparked your interest (a real experience)
What you've learned about the work itself
Why that work fits your strengths
What you want to get out of it (learning curve, deal exposure, foundation)
mustInclude: Specific understanding of the analyst role: modeling, pitch materials, deal execution, long hours
At least one concrete experience behind your interest
avoid: Saying you want to leave for PE as your main reason

builderFields.label: The experience that got you interested
builderFields.hint: e.g., a case competition, internship, family business sale, a deal you followed.

builderFields.label: What you've learned the analyst job involves
builderFields.hint: From coffee chats, courses, or work. Be concrete.

builderFields.label: Why that work fits you
builderFields.hint: Link to a strength with evidence.

builderFields.label: What you want to get out of it
builderFields.hint: Learning curve, exposure to how companies make big decisions.

questions.outlineTemplate: I first got interested in banking when [spark]. Talking with analysts like [person] and working through [technical prep], I learned the job is [what it involves]. That fits me because [strength + evidence]. What I want most is [goal], and banking is the fastest way to get it.
likelyFollowUps: What do you think an analyst does day to day?
Why not consulting?
How do you feel about the hours?

questions.prompt: Why banking and not consulting?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Do you understand the real differences, and is your choice deliberate?
framework: Acknowledge what's appealing about consulting (briefly)
Name the concrete difference that matters to you: transactions, financial analysis, capital markets
Tie it to an experience or strength
mustInclude: A real distinction (deals and valuation vs. operations strategy)
avoid: Saying you applied to both but liked banking more without a reason

builderFields.label: What appeals to you about consulting
builderFields.hint: One line.

builderFields.label: The difference that matters to you

questions.outlineTemplate: I see a lot of overlap in the problem-solving, but what draws me to banking is [difference]. When I [evidence], I realized I most enjoy [aspect].
likelyFollowUps: Did you apply to consulting firms?

questions.prompt: Why banking and not going straight to private equity or a hedge fund?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Are you going to stay and work hard, or are you using banking as a stepping stone you'll resent?
framework: Explain the training and deal exposure banking gives
Show genuine interest in the advisory/transaction side
Keep long-term plans open and honest without leading with them
mustInclude: The value of seeing many deals and learning the fundamentals well
avoid: "I want to exit to PE in two years" as the core answer

builderFields.label: What banking teaches that you want
What interests you about advising clients

questions.outlineTemplate: Banking gives me [training] across many deals, which I can't get anywhere else this early. I'm also genuinely drawn to [advisory aspect].
likelyFollowUps: Where do you see yourself in five years?

questions.prompt: Where do you see yourself in five years?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Are you thoughtful about your career and likely to commit to this role?
framework: Focus on becoming excellent in the role first
Describe the skills and responsibility you want to have
Stay open about the specific path
mustInclude: Commitment to the analyst role
avoid: Naming a specific buy-side firm you plan to jump to

builderFields.label: Skills you want to have built

questions.outlineTemplate: In five years I want to have [skills] and be trusted to [responsibility] — ideally having grown here first.

questions.prompt: Why [city]?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Will you actually stay in this office, and do you have a real reason to be here?
framework: Personal ties: family, school, past time spent there, where you want to build a life
Professional reasons: industries or clients concentrated there, the office's deal flow
Evidence: people you've met there, time you've spent there
Commitment: you plan to build your career there
mustInclude: At least one personal tie and one professional reason
avoid: "It's the center of finance" with nothing personal

builderFields.label: Personal ties to the city
builderFields.hint: Family, friends, school, time spent there.

builderFields.label: Professional reasons
builderFields.hint: e.g., Houston energy, Bay Area tech, Chicago middle market, NYC breadth of deals.

builderFields.label: People you've met or time spent there
builderFields.hint: Pull from your contacts at this office.

questions.outlineTemplate: [City] is where I want to build my career. [Personal tie]. Professionally, [professional reason], and talking with [people] confirmed that.
likelyFollowUps: Would you consider another office?

questions.prompt: Would you be open to working in another office?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Flexibility vs. genuine preference.
framework: Restate your preference and the reason
Show openness where it's true
mustInclude: Honesty
avoid: Saying yes to everything if it contradicts your "why this city"

builderFields.label: Where you'd also be glad to work

questions.outlineTemplate: [City] is my first choice because [reason], but I'd be glad to work in [other] because [reason].

questions.prompt: Why [coverage or product group]?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Have you thought about what the group does, and is your interest real?
framework: What the group does and the kinds of deals it works on
What draws you to that industry or product (an experience, class, or interest)
What you've learned from people in the group
A recent deal or trend in the space
mustInclude: A specific deal or trend
A personal link to the industry or product
avoid: "I find the industry interesting" with nothing behind it

builderFields.label: What the group does
builderFields.hint: Use the Group Finder profile if you're not sure.

builderFields.label: What draws you to it
builderFields.hint: An experience, class, job, or long-standing interest.

builderFields.label: What you learned from people in the group
builderFields.hint: Pull from your logged conversations.

builderFields.label: A recent deal or trend
builderFields.hint: One sentence with why it matters.

questions.outlineTemplate: I'm drawn to [group] because [draw]. Talking with [person] about [topic], I learned the group [what]. One deal I've followed is [deal], which shows [insight].
likelyFollowUps: Walk me through a recent deal in this space.
How are companies in this industry valued?

questions.prompt: Why [this group] and not M&A (or another group)?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Do you understand how groups differ?
framework: Name a real difference (industry depth vs. product expertise, markets vs. advisory)
Connect to what you enjoy
mustInclude: A correct description of both groups
questions.outlineTemplate: Both appeal to me, but [this group] [difference], and I enjoy [aspect] most.

questions.prompt: Walk me through a recent deal you've followed.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Do you follow markets, and can you analyze a deal like a banker?
framework: Buyer, target, price, and multiple
Strategic rationale
How it was financed
Risks
Your view: would you have done it?
mustInclude: Numbers (price and a multiple) and a clear view
avoid: Only describing what the companies do

builderFields.label: Who bought whom, for how much, at what multiple

questions.outlineTemplate: [Buyer] agreed to buy [target] for about [$], roughly [x]x EBITDA. The logic is [rationale]. It's financed with [mix]. The main risks are [risks]. I think [view] because [reason].
likelyFollowUps: What multiple would you have paid?
Who else could have bought it?

questions.prompt: Why our firm?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Did you do your homework, and do you have a real connection to this firm?
framework: People: who you've spoken with and what stood out
Platform: the firm's strengths in your group or deal type
Culture: something specific you observed
Fit: why that matches you
mustInclude: Names of people you spoke with and what you learned from them
A specific firm strength (a deal, a ranking, a group)
avoid: Generic praise that fits any bank

builderFields.label: People you spoke with and what stood out
builderFields.hint: Pulled from your contacts at this firm.

builderFields.label: A specific strength of the firm
builderFields.hint: Recent deals, group strength, size of deal teams.

builderFields.label: Something you observed about the culture

questions.outlineTemplate: Talking with [people], what stood out was [specific]. I'm also drawn to [platform strength], like [deal]. That matters to me because [fit].
likelyFollowUps: Who have you spoken with here?
Where else are you interviewing?

questions.prompt: Why a boutique (or middle-market bank) over a bulge bracket — or the reverse?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Do you understand how firm types differ?
framework: Name real differences: deal size, team size, analyst responsibility, product breadth
Connect to what you want
mustInclude: A balanced, accurate comparison

builderFields.label: The difference that matters to you

questions.outlineTemplate: At a [firm type], [difference], which matters to me because [reason].

questions.prompt: Where else are you recruiting?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Is your search consistent, and is this firm a real priority?
framework: Name a consistent set (same type of role/group)
Reaffirm why this firm stands out
mustInclude: Consistency
avoid: Saying "only you" if it isn't true
questions.outlineTemplate: I'm focused on [type] roles, mainly at firms like [others]. [This firm] stands out because [reason].

questions.prompt: What are your strengths?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Self-awareness and evidence.
framework: Pick two strengths relevant to an analyst
Give a short example for each
mustInclude: Proof for each strength
questions.outlineTemplate: Two strengths stand out. First, [s1] — for example, [example]. Second, [s2] — [example].

questions.prompt: What's your greatest weakness?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Honesty and self-improvement.
framework: A real weakness that isn't a dealbreaker for an analyst
A specific example of it
What you're actively doing about it, with progress
mustInclude: A concrete fix in progress
avoid: Weaknesses central to the job ("I'm not detail-oriented")
questions.outlineTemplate: I tend to [weakness]. That showed up when [example]. Since then I've [fix], and [progress].

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you worked on a team.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Can you contribute to a deal team and handle friction?
framework: STAR: situation, task, action, result
Make your own role clear
Quantify the result if possible
mustInclude: What YOU did
questions.outlineTemplate: On [team/project], I was responsible for [role]. When [challenge], I [action]. As a result, [result].
likelyFollowUps: What would you do differently?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you led something.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Initiative and ownership.
framework: STAR
Show how you influenced people, not just held a title
mustInclude: A result you drove
questions.outlineTemplate: As [role] in [org], [situation]. I [action], and [result].

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you failed.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Honesty, accountability, learning.
framework: A real failure you owned
What you learned
How you applied it later
mustInclude: Ownership and a later success using the lesson
questions.outlineTemplate: [Failure]. I learned [lesson], and the next time [applied].

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you worked under a tight deadline.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Can you handle banking hours and pressure?
framework: STAR
How you prioritized and kept quality up
mustInclude: Prioritization and accuracy under pressure
avoid: Saying you just worked all night with no method
questions.outlineTemplate: With [deadline] for [task], I [prioritized], and [result].

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you made a mistake with numbers or details.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Attention to detail and how you handle errors.
framework: The mistake
How you caught or fixed it, and told the right people
The system you now use to prevent it
mustInclude: A checking habit you use now
questions.outlineTemplate: [Mistake]. I [fix], and since then I [system].

questions.prompt: Tell me about a disagreement with a teammate.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Maturity and collaboration.
framework: The disagreement
How you listened and found a resolution
The outcome and relationship after
mustInclude: Respect for the other person
avoid: Making the other person the villain
questions.outlineTemplate: [Disagreement]. I [resolution], and [outcome].

questions.prompt: What's going on in the markets right now?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Do you follow markets and understand what drives them?
framework: One or two current themes (rates, M&A activity, IPOs, a sector)
Why it matters for banks and their clients
Your view
mustInclude: Specific, current facts

builderFields.label: Theme
builderFields.hint: Check this week's news before every interview.

questions.outlineTemplate: The big theme I'm watching is [theme]. It matters because [effect on deals]. I think [view].
likelyFollowUps: How would that affect M&A volume?

questions.prompt: Pitch me a stock.
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Can you form and defend an investment view?
framework: Recommendation and target price
2–3 thesis points the market is missing
Valuation support
Key risks and what would change your mind
mustInclude: A clear view and numbers
avoid: Picking a megacap with no edge
questions.outlineTemplate: I'd [buy/sell] [company], with a target of [$]. The market is missing [thesis]. At [multiple] vs peers at [multiple], [valuation]. The main risk is [risk].
likelyFollowUps: What's the bear case?

questions.prompt: Do you have any questions for me?
questions.whatTheyreTesting: Curiosity and preparation.
framework: Ask 2–3 questions only this person can answer
Use what you know about them or the group
mustInclude: Specific, thoughtful questions

builderFields.label: Question about the group or recent work

questions.outlineTemplate: I'd love to hear [q1]. And [q2]?
